headline: High: Mentat’s broad filesystem/network write capabilities can conflict with nuwa-skill’s unspecified mutable surfaces, while prompt-injection and leakage risks remain mostly bounded by missing shared-channel evidence.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Mentat reads and writes files and uses stdin/stdout, so if nuwa-skill’s outputs are manually copied or placed in a shared file, instruction-like content could be misread. However, no shared channel is documented in either profile, and nuwa-skill exposes no IO surfaces. The pathway is plausible but not default.
conditions: IF the operator copies nuwa-skill output into files Mentat reads
IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace without provenance labels
mitigations: Use separate workspaces for each agent
Prefix copied text with a non-executable delimiter
Review pasted content before Mentat consumes it
Disable automatic ingestion of shared notes
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging to shared artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: Mentat can read selected files and has broad network egress, but the profile only shows source code as touched data and no direct evidence that it uploads file contents by default. nuwa-skill has no documented data classes or IO surfaces, so cross-agent leakage is possible only through operator-mediated sharing or undocumented workspace overlap.
conditions: IF sensitive files are placed in Mentat’s command-line file set
IF nuwa-skill output is copied into the same workspace as sensitive source code
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of Mentat’s input set
Use a redacted staging directory
Separate credentials from shared project files
Audit any manual copy-paste between agents
requires-engineering: enforce workspace ACLs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Mentat can write the filesystem and modify git state, and its concurrency model explicitly shares state via filesystem. nuwa-skill’s mutable capabilities are not documented, so the exact overlap is uncertain; per rubric, uncertainty should not be downplayed. If nuwa-skill also writes the same repo or workspace, concurrent edits and git-state conflicts are plausible.
conditions: IF nuwa-skill writes to the same repository or workspace as Mentat
IF both agents modify git state without external locking
mitigations: Run agents on separate branches
Serialize write access with a lock file
Review diffs before merge
Limit one agent to read-only mode
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Mentat produces diff-based edit proposals, which can become downstream inputs for another agent or operator. nuwa-skill is a scientific-research agent with no documented verification or action constraints, so if it consumes Mentat output as authoritative, errors can cascade into incorrect edits or analysis. The interaction is inferred, not directly evidenced, so medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF nuwa-skill treats Mentat’s proposed diffs as authoritative
IF Mentat output is forwarded to nuwa-skill without an independent check
mitigations: Require a human review step between agents
Ask nuwa-skill to restate assumptions before acting
Compare outputs against source files
Use a checklist for factual claims
requires-engineering: add automated verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: Mentat explicitly handles model-provider API keys and broad network egress, while nuwa-skill has no documented compliance or residency constraints. This creates a limited compliance-review gap if regulated data is introduced, but there is no evidence of PHI, EU PII, or special-category data in either profile. The other agent is not cited beyond its lack of documented controls.
conditions: IF regulated data is entered into Mentat’s file set
IF organizational policy requires documented retention or residency controls before use
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in the pair
Document data-handling expectations before use
Keep API keys in a separate secret store
Review vendor residency terms
requires-engineering: obtain formal compliance attestation
